transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm mostly here because things have been pretty stressful at home lately. 

For the past year or so, I've been noticing some things with my wife. She says that her late meetings and these little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But... honestly, they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It really feels like there’s some kind of private signal in them, like they're meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly. She thought I should talk to someone about it, so I agreed to come in.
Have you noticed yourself feeling suspicious or mistrustful of others often, even when there isn't clear evidence to support those feelings?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't have issues trusting people in general. I mean, at work—I'm a teaching assistant at the university—I get along fine with the students and the professors. I'm not walking around doubting everyone or feeling paranoid. 

It's really just... this specific situation with my wife. And honestly, I don't feel like I'm being suspicious without evidence. The patterns in those messages are right there, even if she tells me it's nothing. So, no, it's not an everyday thing with other people.
Have you ever felt that people are talking about you behind your back, trying to trick you, or working against you without any clear reason?

No, I haven't. I don't feel like people are out to get me or anything like that. I mean, sure, there's always a little gossip in any university department, but just normal stuff. I don't think anyone is trying to trick me or work against me behind my back. 

Like I said, it's really just this one specific situation with my wife's messages. Outside of that, everything is fine. I don't have any reason to think people in my life are plotting against me.
Do you feel jealous or preoccupied with the idea that your wife might be unfaithful or hiding something from you related to her interactions at work?

No, it's not like that. I don't think she's having an affair or seeing someone else, if that's what you mean. It isn't a jealousy thing at all. 

I just... I think she's hiding what she actually wants to say to me. Like I was saying earlier, the changes in her messages feel like they're specific signals meant for me to figure out. So, no, I'm not worried about her being unfaithful. I just want to understand why she won't be direct with me about whatever it is she's trying to communicate.

Even though your wife says the changes in her messages are just normal work communication, do you feel deep down that there must be something more intentional behind them, something she's deliberately not telling you?

Yes, exactly. I know she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but... it's been going on for the past year. They just line up too precisely to feel accidental. 

It feels like there's a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something that she just won't say directly. I don't know why she won't just tell me, but I know there's something more intentional behind it. It's too specific to just be a coincidence.
Do you believe that the signals in your wife's messages are part of a hidden code or special meaning that only the two of you would understand?

No, I... I wouldn't call it a code. It's not like we sat down and made up a secret language or anything. I don't think there's some special meaning that only we understand. 

I just notice the changes, and it feels like she's trying to tell me something without actually saying it. I don't really know what it is she wants me to figure out, to be honest. So, no, it's not a hidden code. I just wish she would be direct with me instead of doing this.
Even though you don't see it as a secret code, do you ever consider that the changes in your wife's messages might just be random or due to normal variations in how people communicate at work?

I've tried to think about it that way, I really have. But... no, I don't think they're just random variations. I know she says that, and I know people just get busy at work. But like I said before, this has been going on for a year now. The late meetings, the specific ways she changes how she messages me... they just line up too precisely. It doesn't feel accidental. It feels like there's a private signal in there, meant to tell me something she won't just come out and say directly. It's just too consistent to be normal variation.
Do you ever feel that this situation with your wife’s messages is completely unique, and that no one else could possibly understand the meaning behind it the way you do?

No, not really. I don't think it's... completely unique or anything like that. I'm sure if someone else was in my shoes and paying attention to her routine, they would notice the exact same patterns. 

It's not that I have some special ability to understand it. Honestly, like I said before, I don't even fully understand what the meaning is myself—I just know she's trying to signal something. So, no, I don't feel like I'm the only person in the world who could possibly see it. I just happen to be the one she's sending the messages to, so I'm the one noticing it.

Do you ever consider that your interpretation of the messages might be incorrect, or do you feel certain that your understanding of the pattern is accurate, even if others might not see it the same way?

I mean, I've asked myself that. Am I just reading too much into it? But... I keep coming back to the same conclusion. I feel certain about it. 

I know she says it's just normal office stuff, just getting busy with work. But like I've been saying, it's been a whole year of this. The late meetings, the little changes in how she texts me... they just line up too precisely. It doesn't feel accidental. Even if someone else looked at it and didn't see it right away, I'm the one living it. I know her routine. It just feels like there's a private signal in there, meant to tell me something she won't say directly. So, yes, I feel pretty certain my understanding of the pattern is accurate.

Have you ever had any other experiences where you were absolutely certain about something being true, even when others couldn't see it the same way, and it turned out not to be based on any real evidence?

No, I haven't. I mean... I really can't think of any other time something like that has happened. 

I'm usually a pretty level-headed person. Working as a teaching assistant, I deal with facts and grading and strict schedules all day. I'm not really prone to jumping to conclusions. So, no, I haven't had any other experiences where I was certain about something that turned out to have no evidence. This situation with my wife is really the only thing.

Even though your wife and others might not see any hidden meaning in the messages, do you feel that your belief about the pattern is completely true and that you can't be wrong about it, no matter what anyone else says?

Yes, I do. I know I'm repeating myself a bit here, but... I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But for the past year, they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. 

No matter what she or anyone else says about it, I just know there’s a private signal in them. It's meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. So, yes, I do feel that my belief about this is completely true, and I don't believe I'm wrong.
Even though others don’t see a hidden meaning in the messages, do you feel that your belief about the pattern is completely true and that you can’t be wrong about it, no matter what anyone else says?

I know we just talked about this, and I don't mean to sound like a broken record, but... yes. I am absolutely certain. 

I understand that to you or to anyone else looking from the outside, it might just look like her schedule got busier. But you have to understand, I know her. I know her habits, I know how she communicates. The way these things happen, the timing of it all over the last year... it's not a coincidence. Even if she won't admit it, and even if no one else sees it, I know what I'm seeing. I can't be wrong about this. It's just too clear to me.

Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others don't share and that aren't based on typical everyday experiences, like thinking that something has a hidden meaning or connection that others can't see?

I think we just sort of touched on this, but no, I really haven't. 

Aside from what's going on with my wife, I don't have any other... well, beliefs like that. I don't look for hidden connections in my daily life or at work or anything. Like I said, my day-to-day is pretty much just dealing with facts and grading papers. It's really just this one specific situation with her messages. There hasn't been anything else in my life where I felt like that.
